Sam / Priya —

Attached are the validation results from our internal run over your prompt set and holdout queries. Summary highlights below; full CSV attached (acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_results.csv) and the detailed evaluation notebook is on the Drive link.

Summary (rw-rerank-2b baseline vs. rw-rerank-4b-ft candidate):
- NDCG@10 baseline (2b): 0.412
- NDCG@10 candidate (4b-ft): 0.444 (+7.8% relative)
- MRR baseline: 0.287
- MRR candidate: 0.315 (+9.8% relative)
- Latency: baseline 48ms p95, candidate 62ms p95 (both within your 70ms target for the recommended config)

Quality notes / regression risks:
- We saw a small drop in relevance for a narrow set of merchandising queries that rely heavily on business rules. Impact is visible on ~1.2% of queries in the prompt set (examples included in the notebook).
- Recommendation: add a lightweight rule-based override for those SKUs during the A/B (we can supply a suggestion list).

Recommended A/B plan (high-level):
- Traffic: 10% randomization on US organic desktop, 14-day window
- Allocation: 50/50 within the 10% cohort (5% candidate, 5% baseline) to reduce exposure while collecting signal
- Metrics: primary NDCG@10 (stat sig delta), secondary MRR, top-3 CTR; monitor latency p95 and error rate
- Sample size estimate: ~1.2M queries per arm over 14 days (your traffic confirms this is achievable)
- Guardrails: auto-rollback if NDCG@10 drops by >0.5% absolute for candidate vs baseline OR if latency p95 exceeds 75ms on sustained window >30 minutes

Next steps:
1) If you approve the plan, we will push the candidate into a 5% exposure canary and start collecting.
2) We will provide the rule-based override list and an updated prompt filter for the merchandising cases.
3) Post-14-day, we’ll deliver a consolidated A/B report (CSV + notebook) and recommended rollout decision.

Attachments: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_results.csv, ab_test_plan.docx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG-Acme-Rerank

Thanks —
